newsitem.title: UK: Garuda to start London-Batam flights.
newsitem.headline: Garuda to start London-Batam flights.

text.p: Garuda Indonesia will start flying from London to the Indonesian island of Batam on March 30, a route with good cargo potential, the carrier's UK cargo executive Nina Sturrock told Reuters.
The weekly Gatwick-Amman-Batam-Denpasar service will be operated with a passenger McDonnell Douglas MD-11 with an 18 tonne cargo capacity.

Last November, Indonesia's minister of transportation Haryanto Dhanutirto said his government wanted to turn Batam's Hang Nadim airport into an air cargo hub and would make its bilateral arrangements accordingly.
"Ours will be the first direct service from London and the cargo prospects are quite interesting," Sturrock added.
"Batam, 20 km off the coast of Singapore, is also a very leisure orientated island which boasts three golf courses and also has some industrial projects," Sturrock told Reuters.
At present, Garuda flies twice-weekly Gatwick-Jakarta MD-11 services, one of which stops off at Abu Dhabi en route and the other at Amman.
"We do not have (drop-off/pick-up) passenger or cargo traffic rights at either Abu Dhabi or Amman at present, although we are working on securing these with Jordan at least," she added.
She added that Garuda had made no decision on whether to increase its ex-UK cargo rates in line with the normal spring policy adopted by many airlines.
